_link.title: I can compare the CNS and PNS in terms of the types of neurons each contains

toLevel2.stem: Which type of neuron makes up the central nervous system?
Which types of neurons make up the peripheral nervous system?
The spinal cord is part of which division of the nervous system?
Which neurons are found in the spinal cord?
Which two structures make up the central nervous system?
distractors: The spinal cord and motor nerves

toLevel2.stem: The CNS is made up of interneurons, while the PNS is made up of sensory and motor neurons.
The spinal cord contains sensory and motor neurons because it connects to peripheral nerves.
The central nervous system is made up of {{blank:1}}, while the peripheral nervous system is made up of sensory and motor neurons.
The spinal cord is part of the {{blank:1}} and therefore contains interneurons.
The PNS contains {{blank:1}} neurons that carry messages toward the CNS and {{blank:2}} neurons that carry messages away from the CNS.

toLevel3.stem: Why is it incorrect to say the spinal cord contains sensory neurons?
toLevel3.answer: The spinal cord is part of the CNS, which contains interneurons
distractors: Sensory neurons do not exist anywhere in the nervous system
The spinal cord is part of the PNS, not the central system
Sensory neurons are only found inside the brain structure

toLevel3.stem: How do interneurons in the CNS relate to sensory and motor neurons in the PNS?
toLevel3.answer: Interneurons process and relay information between them
distractors: Interneurons replace sensory and motor neurons over time
Interneurons and PNS neurons perform identical functions
Interneurons only connect to other interneurons in the CNS

toLevel3.stem: Why does the CNS contain interneurons rather than sensory or motor neurons?
toLevel3.answer: The CNS processes information rather than detecting or responding
distractors: Interneurons are larger and cannot fit in peripheral structures
Sensory and motor neurons cannot survive inside the spinal cord
The CNS does not need to communicate with any other structures

toLevel3.stem: A student claims that motor neurons are found in the spinal cord because motor commands originate there. Why is this reasoning incorrect?
toLevel3.answer: The spinal cord contains interneurons; motor neurons are in the PNS
distractors: Motor commands do not originate in the spinal cord at all
The spinal cord is part of the PNS and contains motor neurons
Motor neurons are found in both the CNS and PNS equally

toLevel3.stem: What is the key distinction between the neuron types found in the CNS and those found in the PNS?
toLevel3.answer: The CNS has interneurons; the PNS has sensory and motor neurons
distractors: The CNS has motor neurons; the PNS has only interneurons
The CNS has sensory neurons; the PNS has only interneurons
Both divisions contain all three neuron types in equal numbers

toLevel3.stem: Why is it important to know that the brain contains interneurons rather than sensory or motor neurons?
toLevel3.answer: It clarifies the brain's role in processing, not detecting or responding
distractors: The brain does not actually communicate with any other structures
Sensory and motor neurons cannot function inside the skull cavity
The brain is part of the PNS, so it uses different neuron types

toLevel3.stem: Interneurons in the CNS process and relay information between sensory and motor neurons in the PNS.
The CNS contains interneurons because its role is to {{blank:1}} information, not to detect stimuli or produce physical responses.
A common student error is stating that the spinal cord contains {{blank:1}} neurons, when it actually contains interneurons because it is part of the CNS.
Interneurons in the CNS {{blank:1}} information between the sensory and motor neurons located in the PNS.

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam question asks: 'Which neurons make up the spinal cord?' Liam answers 'sensory neurons.' Why is his answer incorrect?
toLevel4.answer: The spinal cord is part of the CNS and contains interneurons
distractors: Sensory neurons are not real; they are called afferent neurons
The spinal cord is part of the PNS and contains motor neurons
Sensory neurons are only found inside the brain, not the cord

toLevel4.stem: Maya is tracing the neural pathway of a conscious response. She identifies that sensory neurons carry information to the spinal cord. Which type of neuron would then carry the message within the spinal cord?
A student writes: 'Motor neurons in the brain send commands to the muscles.' How should this be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: The brain contains interneurons; motor neurons are in the PNS
distractors: The statement is correct because the brain uses motor neurons
Motor neurons are only found in the spinal cord, not the brain
The brain contains sensory neurons that send commands to muscles

toLevel4.stem: In a spinal reflex, the sensory neuron carries a signal to the spinal cord. Which neuron type receives this signal within the spinal cord?
Tom is asked to identify which neurons are found in the arm. He should identify which of the following?
A diagram shows a neural pathway from a receptor in the skin to the brain. Which neuron type would be located in the brain according to this pathway?
Ella is writing an exam answer about the PNS. She needs to name the neuron types found there. Which answer is correct?
distractors: All three types: sensory, motor, and interneurons

toLevel4.stem: When Liam answers that the spinal cord contains sensory neurons, his error is that the spinal cord is part of the {{blank:1}} and therefore contains {{blank:2}}.
In a spinal reflex, the signal is received within the spinal cord by an {{blank:1}}, which then relays it to a motor neuron in the {{blank:2}}.
Neurons found in the arm are part of the {{blank:1}} and include sensory and motor neurons, not interneurons.

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that the spinal cord must contain motor neurons because it sends commands to muscles. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the spinal cord contains interneurons that relay to PNS motor neurons
distractors: Correct; the spinal cord directly sends commands using its own motor neurons
Correct; motor neurons are found in both the CNS and the PNS equally
Incorrect; the spinal cord only contains sensory neurons not motor neurons

toLevel5.stem: A textbook states that 'all three types of neurons are found throughout the entire nervous system.' Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the CNS has interneurons and the PNS has sensory and motor neurons
distractors: Correct; every part of the nervous system contains all three neuron types
Correct; the distribution of neurons is uniform across all divisions
Incorrect; only one type of neuron exists in the entire nervous system

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee claims that interneurons are found only in the brain and not in the spinal cord. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; interneurons are in both the brain and spinal cord
distractors: Correct; interneurons are exclusive to the brain structure only
Correct; the spinal cord contains sensory and motor neurons only
Incorrect; interneurons are found only in the spinal cord region

toLevel5.stem: A student writes: 'Sensory neurons are in the PNS because they detect stimuli, and interneurons are in the CNS because they process information.' Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Accurate; the neuron types match each division's function
distractors: Incorrect; sensory neurons are also found within the CNS
Incorrect; interneurons detect stimuli, not sensory neurons
Accurate; but motor neurons should be in the CNS as well

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that because sensory neurons connect to the spinal cord, sensory neurons must be part of the CNS. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; connecting to the CNS does not make them part of it
distractors: Correct; any neuron connected to the CNS is classified as CNS
Correct; sensory neurons become interneurons when they reach the cord
Incorrect; sensory neurons do not connect to the spinal cord at all

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that the distinction between CNS and PNS neuron types is irrelevant because all neurons perform the same function. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; each type has a distinct role that matches its division's function
distractors: Correct; all neurons are structurally and functionally identical
Correct; the division of neuron types is purely an academic convention
Incorrect; only interneurons perform any meaningful neural function

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that the brain must contain sensory neurons because it receives sensory information. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sensory neurons deliver information to the CNS but are located in the PNS
distractors: Correct; the brain contains sensory neurons that receive peripheral messages
Correct; receiving sensory information means sensory neurons must be present
Incorrect; the brain does not receive any sensory information from the body

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that the PNS must also contain interneurons because complex processing occurs in peripheral ganglia. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: At VCE level, interneurons are classified as belonging to the CNS
distractors: Correct; interneurons are equally distributed across CNS and PNS
Incorrect; no processing of any kind occurs in the PNS structures
Correct; ganglia contain all three neuron types in equal proportions

toLevel5.stem: The argument that the spinal cord contains motor neurons is {{blank:1}} because the spinal cord is part of the CNS and contains {{blank:2}}.
The claim that all three neuron types are found throughout the nervous system is {{blank:1}} because the CNS and PNS contain {{blank:2}} types of neurons.
